skill.name: slb
skill.description: SLB adds a two-person approval workflow before AI agents run risky shell commands. It documents risk tiers, command hashing, review gates, rollback options, hooks, and audit workflows for a Go CLI.
skill.summary: Add peer approval and audit logging before risky AI agent commands execute.
skill.author: Dicklesworthstone

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are documentation examples, Markdown fences, configuration samples, or UI output and were marked false positive. Confirmed risks remain for remote installer execution, arbitrary command execution in the user environment, emergency override paths, hook configuration writes, TCP exposure, and sensitive local state. No prompt injection language was found in the skill file.

remediation.issue: Remote install command pipes a downloaded script directly to bash.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the one-liner with a pinned release, checksum verification, and a separate inspect-before-run installation path.

remediation.issue: Approved commands inherit powerful local and cloud credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Document least-privilege setup, isolated shells, test credentials, and explicit human review for critical tiers.

remediation.issue: Emergency override can bypass the normal peer approval workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Make emergency override opt-in, disable non-interactive use by default, and require post-incident review logs.

remediation.issue: Daemon TCP examples can expose SLB beyond the local machine.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer Unix sockets or loopback binding, and require authentication plus narrow allow-lists for remote use.

remediation.issue: Hook and IDE integration commands write agent configuration files.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation, show diffs, create backups, and document how to uninstall hooks safely.

semantic_findings.title: Arbitrary Command Execution In Inherited User Environment
semantic_findings.description: The skill states that commands run in the user shell and inherit AWS, Kubernetes, SSH, and database credentials, while SLB can run arbitrary command text after approval. This makes reviewer compromise or mistaken approval high impact.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly describes inherited credentials and a generic command execution flow. This is core intended behavior, but the security impact is direct and clear.

semantic_findings.title: Emergency Override Bypasses Peer Approval Controls
semantic_findings.description: The emergency override section allows humans to bypass normal approval, including a non-interactive acknowledgment path. This creates a deliberate bypass for the two-person control that must be tightly restricted.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The section names emergency override and documents both interactive and non-interactive execution paths. It also states the bypass is for emergencies, confirming the business-logic risk.

content.user_title: Guard Destructive AI Commands with Peer Review
content.value_statement: AI agents can run destructive shell commands before a human notices. SLB adds peer approval, command hashing, and audit logs before risky commands execute.
actual_capabilities: Classifies shell commands into safe, caution, dangerous, and critical tiers.
Requires peer approval before dangerous or critical commands execute.
Binds approvals to command hashes to detect command changes.
Documents session management, review, rollback, daemon, TUI, and hook workflows.
Supports audit history, outcome tracking, and event streaming for reviewers.
limitations: The skill is documentation for an external Go CLI, not the CLI implementation itself.
Commands still run in the user shell with the user credentials and permissions.
Safety depends on correct pattern configuration and trustworthy reviewers.
Emergency override and auto-approve modes can reduce the approval protection.

use_cases.title: Review destructive DevOps actions
use_cases.description: Require another agent or human to approve risky deployment, Kubernetes, Terraform, or database commands.

use_cases.title: Coordinate multi-agent coding sessions
use_cases.description: Create a shared approval workflow when several Claude, Codex, or Claude Code agents work in one repository.

use_cases.title: Audit risky automation
use_cases.description: Record who requested, reviewed, approved, executed, or rejected high-impact commands.

prompt_templates.title: Start a guarded session
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one agent terminal.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me start an SLB session for this project and explain what information reviewers need before approving commands.

prompt_templates.title: Classify a planned command
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the SLB guidance to classify this command, explain the risk tier, and suggest safer dry-run checks first: <command>.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a review request
prompt_templates.scenario: Create reviewer context for a dangerous operation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an SLB request reason for this risky operation, including scope, rollback plan, and evidence a reviewer should inspect: <operation>.

prompt_templates.title: Audit approval policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this SLB configuration for weak approval settings, unsafe network exposure, auto-approval risk, and emergency override controls: <configuration>.

output_examples.input: Classify a command that removes a build directory.
output_examples.output: The command is dangerous because it deletes files recursively. Request approval, include why the directory is safe to remove, and confirm backups are not needed.

output_examples.input: Review an SLB configuration with a remote daemon enabled.
output: Network exposure should be limited to trusted interfaces.
Authentication must stay enabled for TCP mode.
Reviewers should reject requests without a clear rollback plan.

output_examples.output: Use emergency override only for active incidents. Include the exact command, the incident reason, expected impact, approval record, and post-incident review steps.

best_practices: Use least-privilege cloud, Kubernetes, SSH, and database credentials before running SLB commands.
Require human review for critical tiers and disable non-interactive emergency override where possible.
Prefer dry-run, diff, backup, and rollback capture before approving destructive commands.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote installers directly to a shell in production environments.
Do not let the same agent request and approve destructive work without a delay or human review.
Do not expose the daemon on all interfaces unless authentication, allow-lists, and network controls are verified.

faq.question: Does SLB execute commands on a remote server?
faq.answer: No. The documentation says commands run in the user shell, while the daemon verifies approvals.

faq.question: Can SLB prevent every destructive mistake?
faq.answer: No. It adds review gates, but credentials, backups, access controls, and reviewer judgment remain important.

faq.question: Why are dangerous commands shown in the skill?
faq.answer: They are examples used to explain risk tiers and approval behavior. They should not be run without review.

faq.question: Is this skill suitable for Claude Code and Codex workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents workflows for Claude Code hooks, Codex-style terminals, and multi-agent command review.

faq.question: What should reviewers check before approval?
faq.answer: Reviewers should check command scope, dry-run output, rollback options, credentials, and the reason for execution.

faq.question: What is the main security concern?
faq.answer: Approved commands inherit the user environment, so unsafe approval can affect local files, cloud resources, and infrastructure.
